mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions that reduce corporate investment and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's returns (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS increases <0.25% in all months during the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) below the prior month's level, accompanied by a decline in the monthly index of industrial production (INDPRO), predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as weak labor market indicators coincide with supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < previous month AND INDPRO < previous month
regime_hint: Labor market softening coupled with supply contraction
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of months when the trigger occurs, or the correlation between the combined labor/supply signal and returns is < -0.2.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in housing starts (HOUST) by at least 10% in a month is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals renewed consumer and builder confidence, prompting equity market optimism.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥10% in a month
failure_condition: Across 5 such months, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior month's returns (t-test p > 0.05), or HOUST increases are <10% in all months.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly industrial production index (INDPRO) falls by more than 5% from the prior month, the S&P 500 5-day forward return turns negative due to expectations of persistent supply-side shocks and reduced corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by >5% from previous month
failure_condition: In 10 such events, the 5-day forward returns are not negative (mean > 0) or the average return magnitude is below the pre-shock mean by less than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: During a period when the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% in three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to anticipated inflationary pressure and rate hike anticipation.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in each of 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 8 such 3-month inflation windows, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or inflation decelerates by ≥0.3% in the subsequent month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.0% and a sharp rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 indicate a strong labor market, which predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investor sentiment improves.
regime_hint: Labor market strengthening with robust hiring
failure_condition: Across 10 such labor-market events, the 60-day forward returns are negative in >50% of cases, or the interaction effect between UNRATE and PAYEMS is statistically insignificant (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in retail sales (captured by a proxy such as GDPC1 growth > 2%) predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it reflects robust consumer demand and optimism about future earnings.
failure_condition: In 8 such months, the 20-day forward returns are not higher than the prior month's return (mean difference ≤ 0), or GDPC1 growth is not definitively identified as a distinct series in the data.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of new home construction to prior month (HOUST) falls by 15% or more, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent housing market weakness and its spillover to consumer and business sentiment.
failure_condition: Over 12 such contractions, the 60-day forward returns are not consistently negative (mean < -0.5%), or HOUST recovers by ≥15% in the following month in all cases.
